claims.text: HFrEF: now second-line, for patients who can't take an ARNI (intolerance, unavailable, cost).
claims.quote: In patients with HFrEF, their current role is as a second-line agent for those who cannot tolerate ARNi or those for whom ARNi is not available, cost-prohibitive, or otherwise unfeasible.

claims.text: Stop the ACE inhibitor 36 hours before starting sacubitril/valsartan.
claims.quote: ACE inhibitors should be discontinued 36 hours before initiation of sacubitril/valsartan.

claims.text: Lisinopril for HF: start 5 mg once daily, increase as tolerated to 40 mg daily.
claims.quote: Heart Failure: Initiate with 5 mg once daily. Increase dose as tolerated to 40 mg daily ( 2.2 )

claims.text: Check electrolytes and renal function before starting, at 1 month, and after each significant dose increase or clinical change;
claims.quote: Serum electrolytes and renal function should be measured before an ACE inhibitor is initiated, at 1 month, and after each significant increase in dose or change in clinical condition.

claims.text: reduce or hold the dose during dehydration or acute renal decline.
claims.quote: If dehydration or poor renal function due to acute illness develops, the ACE inhibitor dose may need to be reduced or temporarily discontinued.

claims.text: Lisinopril: K-sparing diuretics raise hyperkalemia risk;
claims.quote: Potassium-sparing diuretics (spironolactone, amiloride, triamterene, and others) can increase the risk of hyperkalemia.

claims.text: NSAIDs raise renal-impairment risk and blunt the BP effect;
claims.quote: NSAIDS: Increased risk of renal impairment and loss of antihypertensive efficacy ( 7.3 )

claims.text: lithium toxicity has been reported (monitor lithium levels);
claims.quote: Lithium toxicity has been reported in patients receiving lithium concomitantly with drugs, which cause elimination of sodium, including ACE inhibitors.
Zestril is contraindicated in combination with a neprilysin inhibitor (e.g., sacubitril).
Do not co-administer aliskiren with ZESTRIL in patients with diabetes

claims.text: Lisinopril overdose: hypotension is most likely, treated with IV normal saline;
claims.quote: The most likely manifestation of overdosage would be hypotension, for which the usual treatment would be intravenous infusion of normal saline solution.

claims.text: lisinopril can be removed by hemodialysis.
claims.quote: Lisinopril can be removed by hemodialysis
